content.text: In Zimbabwe, where the local currency collapsed and international payment platforms like Stripe rejected businesses, COREMERCH rose to fill the gap with sovereign digital commerce stacks that empower creators to own their infrastructure, process crypto payments without relying on conventional platforms, and scale their businesses without borders. This guide will walk you through building a crypto store on [[LINK:https://coremerch.[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/github-pages-free-digital-product-store-hosting-what-3|GitHub Pages]].io/store/blog/[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-r2-digital-product-storage-delivery-what-actually-2|COREMERCH guide to cloudflare]]-workers-crypto-payment-webhooks-what-actually-how|cloudflare]] Pages, with or without Stripe, and deploying it with the Sovereign Starter Stack ($97) or Edge Commerce Stack ($197).
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

Traditional digital commerce stacks often rely on centralized payment gateways like Stripe, which can reject businesses due to country or platform restrictions, leaving them without a means to process payments. By using sovereign digital commerce stacks, creators can build their own infrastructure and process crypto payments directly, eliminating reliance on third-party platforms and giving them full control over their business operations.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Stack 02 — the Edge Commerce Stack — uses Cloudflare Pages for storefront hosting, Cloudflare Workers for backend webhook handling, Supabase for order storage, Cloudflare R2 for product file delivery, and Resend for transactional email. The entire stack costs nothing per month up to significant volume thresholds — Cloudflare Workers provides 100,000 requests per day free, Supabase provides 500MB of PostgreSQL storage free, Cloudflare R2 provides 10GB storage and zero egress fees free, and Resend provides 3,000 emails per month free. SPF, DKIM, and DMARC are configured during COREMERCH deployment.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

To set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you'll need to create a new account with NOWPayments and configure it as your payment gateway. You'll also need to set up a delivery pipeline using Cloudflare Workers to handle file delivery and storage. Once you have your payment and delivery pipeline set up, you can integrate it with your crypto store.
By using sovereign digital commerce stacks, creators can build their own infrastructure and process crypto payments directly, eliminating reliance on third-party platforms.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Testing before promotion is not optional — it is the step that determines whether your store functions correctly under real conditions before real buyers encounter it. The test sequence has four steps. First: deploy the backend and confirm the webhook endpoint returns a valid response to a test HTTP POST. Second: configure the storefront and confirm the checkout displays correctly on desktop and mobile. Third: complete a real mainnet transaction with a small amount of actual crypto. Fourth: check your order database and confirm the order was logged correctly, the delivery email arrived, and the download link works.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

The post-deployment ownership transfer is explicit in every COREMERCH deployment. When the build is complete and the end-to-end test passes, COREMERCH provides the credentials and configuration details for every component under the customer's accounts. The GitHub or Cloudflare repository is under the customer's account from the start. The Supabase or Google Sheets database is under the customer's account. The NOWPayments account is under the customer's email. COREMERCH removes collaborator access upon delivery. From that point, the store runs entirely under the customer's own accounts.
How do I build a digital store that accepts crypto payments for free?

The setup sequence matters because each component depends on the previous one being correctly configured. Start with NOWPayments: create your account, configure wallet addresses for each coin you want to accept, generate the API key, and note the IPN secret key you will set. Then configure the backend: in Stack 01, deploy the Google Apps Script Web App and note its URL; in Stack 02, deploy the Cloudflare Worker and note its URL. Set that URL as the webhook endpoint in your NOWPayments IPN settings. Then configure the storefront. Then run a real mainnet test — send actual crypto to your configured wallet address, confirm NOWPayments detects it, confirm the webhook fires, and confirm the delivery email arrives with a working download link.
Cloudflare Workers allow for customization of the payment and delivery pipeline, providing a unique and tailored solution for business needs.
Related: How Creators Like You Are Building Sovereign Stores

For more information on deploying a digital product store, check out our Edge Commerce Stack ($197), which includes Cloudflare Pages + Workers + Supabase + NOWPayments and is deployed in 48 hours, end-to-end tested before handoff. You can also browse our products at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html. Additionally, our Edge Commerce Stack is a great option for those looking for a more comprehensive solution for their digital product store.
Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy your crypto store, follow these steps: Create a Cloudflare Pages account and set up a new site; Create a GitHub repository for your project and link it to Cloudflare Pages; Install the Cloudflare Workers SDK and NOWPayments library; Set up a payment gateway with NOWPayments; Configure a delivery pipeline using Cloudflare Workers; Integrate your payment and delivery pipeline with your crypto store; Deploy your crypto store and go live.
